title: RPG Maker FES Sprites are too large.

posts.author: Scion_of_the_Shadowlight
posts.body:
I got the rpg maker FES resource pack for my game, its very nice but the sprites are way too big! It bugs me because i do want to use them, and use custom characters/mz characters as important npc's, but the sprites are so much bigger, does anyone have a good idea of what editor i should use to shrink them?
(Dont mind the purple circle and squares, they are simply collision detection.)

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: By characters you mean the character sprites on map? If yes, then they are supposed to fit 24x24 grid size, and default one for RMMZ is 48x48, so how they can be too big? For image editing, you can use GIMP for example.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Your screenshot is a little blurry, so it's hard to tell, but you might be lucky.
The oversized sprites seem to be scaled, so every pixel is actually 2x2 or 3x3 pixels. If you scale them down in a graphics program by that factor, and without a smoothing method, you should be able to resize them without quality loss. But they might be a lot smaller than the other chars afterwards.

posts.author: Emily Frost
posts.body:
When I have a lot of images to convert or change I use a program called
Multiple Image Resizer .NET
​
".net" is part of the name, by the way, like Paint dot net, its not a website its just the name of the program. Anyway, its free and easily available by a simple google search. It resizes however you like with or without transparancy and without quality loss and you can resize an entire folder or as many pictures as you like at one time. Pretty easy to pick up and use.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Emily Frost said:
It resizes however you like with or without [...] quality loss
Click to expand...
technically untrue, especially when we are talking about pixel art where even a 1% decrease in size can be difficult for a resize algorithm to resolve how to reposition or fill pixels when we are dealing with a very limited resolution.
Where do the pixels go when you decrease the size? There has to be some sort of quality loss.
To me, this software looks sketchy, and I recommend just using GIMP/Photoshop to resize.

If we are solely speaking on quality loss, then of course there is quality loss. There has to be because you cannot magically make the pixels on your computer monitor smaller to fit more detail.
There has to be quality loss. It does seem softer overall and some of the finer details (such as the belts) begin to blend or even disappear into the uniform.
However, there isn't much you can do about it. When you are developing there are going to be times you may just have to make compromises like this.
I often use a zoom effect in my game to a non-integer scale. I am aware it does alter the quality of the pixel art when I do it, but I feel the quality loss is a worthwhile trade off to have a more dynamic camera. That's a compromise I've made.
So as Kenen said:

If you're satisfied, then more power to you.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
As said before, the (original) assets are scaled by x2, so each pixel is actually 2x2 pixels. So they can be down scaled by 50% without quality loss. Everything else will end up in blurry/squished/distorted/merged pixels.
But keep on going and experiment with that stuff. Make your experiences. If your game reaches a certain stage in development, you'll have enough time to reconsider, if these assets are what you want.

What do you mean by it looks sketchy lol?
Its not a new program. Its been around at least twenty years and is free and has no ads. Photoshop is the one trying to get your money not this open program. Its truly very good. But moreover, both gimp and photoshop are not designed to resize images, it is merely a task they are capable of doing. So the interface to do so is somewhat buried in their menu interface. On the other hand, the Multiple Image Resizer program is very simple for a person with without editing experience to utilize because it is designed with resizing and/or cropping as its premiere function so the method to do this is at the forefront of the interface.
So for a person that asks specifically about resizing images, I would again definitely recommend it. It also has a little side by side view so he/she can see what the output image will look like at the same time as the input image. You should give it a whirl too! You might become a believer!
